definition_zh: 星座；星群；（相关的）一组事物；群星般的一批人物；卫星星座
definition_en: a group of stars forming a recognized pattern, or a group of related things or people
core_image: 几张亮星之间被想象出的细线连起来，夜空上浮出一幅猎人的轮廓
scene: 夜里辨认天上连成图案的一组星，你说 Those seven bright points form a constellation.
sceneCN: 这里 constellation 指「被认作一个图案的一组星」（第 1 个义项：肉眼连成的星群图形）；句意为那七个亮点构成一个星座。图中可辨识物件：七颗亮星、连线的想象轮廓、星图、指星的手。

pos.zh: 星座；星群；一组相关事物；一批人物；卫星星座

forms.label: 相关动词（使聚成星群，少用）

derivatives.zh: constellation 同出拉丁 constellare：使聚成星群；非由本词加后缀，而是同一词族的动词
stella + -ar：恒星的；与本词共享 stella 词根
希腊 aster + -ism：较小的星群图形；与本词并列的天文术语

senses.title: A pattern of stars
senses.titleCN: 天上被认作一个图案的一组星
senses.definition: a group of stars that observers join into a recognizable pattern
senses.definitionCN: 观测者连成一个可辨认图案的一组恒星
senses.example: Those seven bright points form a constellation.
senses.exampleCN: 那七个亮点构成一个星座。
senses.why: the word is built from com- 'together' and stella 'star', so its plain sense is simply stars gathered into one figure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 com-「共同」与 stella「星」构成，本义就是被聚成同一个图形的一群星。

senses.title: A bounded region of the sky
senses.definition: one of the eighty-eight regions into which modern astronomy divides the whole sky
senses.definitionCN: 现代天文学把全天划成的八十八个区域之一
senses.example: Every star lies inside exactly one constellation.
senses.exampleCN: 每颗恒星都恰好落在一个星座的边界内。
senses.why: once star charts needed unambiguous addresses, the drawn figure was replaced by a region with borders, and the old word kept the new job.
senses.whyCN: 当星图需要没有歧义的地址时，画出的图形被换成有边界的区域，旧词承担了新任务。

senses.title: A sign of the zodiac
senses.titleCN: 黄道十二宫中的一个宫
senses.definition: one of the twelve traditional star groups through which the sun appears to pass
senses.definitionCN: 太阳视运动所经的十二个传统星群之一
senses.example: In astrology a constellation names a sign, not a region.
senses.exampleCN: 在占星里，constellation 指一个宫，而非天区。
senses.why: astrology froze twelve of the old figures into a system of signs, so the word carries a second, non-astronomical sense.
senses.whyCN: 占星把其中十二个旧图形冻结成宫位体系，因此这个词带有第二个非天文的义项。

senses.title: A group of related things
senses.titleCN: 一组彼此关联的事物（如症状）
senses.definition: a set of related things that appear together, such as symptoms or factors
senses.definitionCN: 一同出现的一组相关事物，如症状或因素
senses.example: The doctor recognized a constellation of symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 医生认出这是一组相关症状。
senses.why: the sky image is reused whenever separate items are seen as one figure, because the mind joins them the way it joins stars.
senses.whyCN: 只要彼此分开的事物被看成一个图形，这个天空意象就会被重用，因为心智连线的方式与连星一样。

senses.title: A gathering of eminent people
senses.definition: a group of famous or talented people gathered in one place or field
senses.definitionCN: 聚集在同一场合或领域的一批有名或才华出众的人
senses.example: The gala drew a constellation of scientists.
senses.exampleCN: 这场盛会聚集了一批科学家。
senses.why: the metaphor is social: a room full of distinguished people looks like a sky full of bright stars.
senses.whyCN: 这是社交比喻：一屋子显赫的人物，看起来就像满天亮星。

senses.title: A network of satellites
senses.titleCN: 卫星星座：一组协同工作的卫星
senses.definition: a group of satellites working together in coordinated orbits
senses.definitionCN: 在协调轨道上协同工作的一组卫星
senses.example: A low-orbit constellation can cover the whole planet.
senses.exampleCN: 低轨卫星星座可以覆盖整个行星。
senses.why: engineers borrowed the word because the satellites, like stars, are many separate points that only make sense as one pattern.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用这个词，因为卫星正如星星：许多分开的点，只有作为一个图形才有意义。

senses.title: The naming grid of the sky
senses.titleCN: 天文命名法：星座名作恒星名的属格部分
senses.definition: the naming system in which a star is labelled by a letter or number plus the genitive of its constellation
senses.definitionCN: 用一个字母或数字加星座名的属格来标记恒星的命名体系
senses.example: Alpha Centauri is the brightest star of the constellation Centaurus.
senses.exampleCN: 南门二是半人马座中最亮的星。
senses.why: because a star needed an address before it had a name, the constellation became the surname in the label.
senses.whyCN: 因为恒星在有名之前先需要一个地址，星座就成了标签里的姓。

senses.title: A fixed configuration of circumstances
senses.titleCN: 比喻义：一组固定的因素组合
senses.definition: a particular arrangement of circumstances or forces seen as a single pattern
senses.definitionCN: 被视为一个整体图形的一组境况或力量
senses.example: A rare constellation of interests made the treaty possible.
senses.exampleCN: 各种利益罕见地凑成一种组合，使条约成为可能。
senses.why: the abstract sense generalizes the visual one: any set of elements that only works when arranged together is a constellation.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把视觉义一般化：任何只有在这样排列时才成立的一组要素，都是一个星座。

intro.en: Constellation comes from Late Latin constellatio 'a gathering of stars', built on com- 'together' and stella 'star'. It reached English through Old French and later split into an astronomical and an astrological sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: constellation 出自晚期拉丁 constellatio「聚在一起的星」，由 com-「共同」与 stella「星」构成。它经古法语进入英语，后来分成天文学与占星两个义项。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stella 'star' is the Latin noun behind the whole family; it is a cognate of English star, not its source, and both go back to a reconstructed Indo-European root.
items.cn: stella 是「星」的拉丁名词，是整个词族的根基；它与英语 star 同源而非其来源，两者都出自一个印欧重构词根。

items.en: The prefix com- 'together, with' turns a single star into a set of stars seen as one thing.
items.cn: 前缀 com-「共同、一起」把单颗星变成被看成一体的一个星集。

items.en: Constellatio named a set of stars, and the related adjective constellatus 'set with stars' shows the same image of stars studding a field.
items.cn: constellatio 指一组星，相关形容词 constellatus「布满星的」显示同一意象：星点布满一片区域。

items.en: Old French constellation carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century, when it still covered both the pattern and its astrological use.
items.cn: 古法语 constellation 在 13 世纪把这个名词带进英语，当时它同时涵盖图形与占星用途。

items.en: In 1922 the International Astronomical Union adopted a list of eighty-eight constellations, and in 1930 formal boundaries were published, turning figures into regions.
items.cn: 1922 年国际天文联合会通过八十八个星座的名单，1930 年公布了正式边界，把图形变成了区域。

items.en: Root uncertainty: the derivation through a hypothetical verb constellare is generally believed but that verb is sparsely attested, so the intermediate step is a reconstruction. First-date uncertainty only: the earliest English use of the noun is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 词根存疑：经假想动词 constellare 的派生一般认为成立，但该动词书证稀少，因此中间环节属重构。仅首见年代存疑：这个名词最早的英语用例没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds the sky terms most often confused with constellation; group two holds the borrowed uses for groups of things and people.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易与 constellation 混淆的天空术语；第二组是借用来说「一组事物、一批人」的近义说法。

entries.definition: A recognized pattern that is not one of the eighty-eight official regions, such as the Big Dipper; astronomers keep the two terms apart.
entries.definitionCN: 不属于八十八个正式区域的可辨图形，如北斗七星；天文学家把这两个词分开用。

entries.definition: Greek gala 'milk' gave the name of our own star system; a galaxy contains many constellations, so the words work at different scales.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊 gala「奶」给出我们所在星系的名称；一个星系包含许多星座，两词尺度不同。

entries.definition: The belt of twelve traditional signs; it is a system built from constellations, not a synonym for one of them.
entries.definitionCN: 十二个传统宫位构成的带；它是由星座构成的体系，并非某一个星座的同义词。

entries.definition: A general word for things grouped closely; it says nothing about a pattern, which is what constellation adds.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指聚在一起的一组；它不含「图案」之意，而这正是 constellation 增添的。

entries.definition: A formal word for a collection of items; constellation is more figurative and suggests the items form a figure.
entries.definitionCN: 指收集成组之物的正式用语；constellation 更偏比喻，暗示这些事物构成一个图形。

entries.definition: A set arranged for a purpose, as in an array of sensors; it stresses arrangement, not the picture the arrangement makes.
entries.definitionCN: 为某一目的排布的一组，如传感器阵列；它强调排列，而非排列造成的图像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + stella 'star': stars gathered into one figure.
normal.cn: com-「共同」+ stella「星」：被聚成一个图形的星。

normal.en: Modern astronomy counts eighty-eight constellations.
normal.cn: 现代天文学把全天划成八十八个星座。

normal.en: A star's label uses the constellation as a surname: Alpha Centauri.
normal.cn: 恒星的名字把星座当姓：南门二。

normal.en: Borrowed collocations: a constellation of symptoms, of talent.
normal.cn: 借用搭配：一组症状、一批人才。

normal.en: The family runs stellar, constellate, asterism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 stellar、constellate、asterism。

abstract.en: Picture separate lamps in a dark room joined by an imaginary line.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里几盏分开的灯被一条想象中的线连起来。

abstract.en: Picture a party where every guest is a small light and the room becomes a sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一场聚会，每位客人都是一个小光点，房间成了天空。

abstract.en: Picture a map with borders drawn around a shape that used to be just a picture.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，围绕一个原本只是图形的轮廓画上了边界。

examples.en: The constellation Orion is visible on winter evenings.
examples.cn: 猎户座在冬季夜晚可见。

examples.en: Doctors look for a constellation of signs before diagnosing.
examples.cn: 医生在确诊前会寻找一组相关体征。

examples.en: The company plans a constellation of small satellites.
examples.cn: 该公司计划建一个小卫星星座。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ stell（星）+ ation」——许多星被聚在一起 → 星座；引申为一组相关事物

root: 晚期拉丁 constellatio「聚在一起的星」= com-「共同」+ stella「星」+ -atio（名词后缀）；stella 与英语 star、希腊 aster 同源。经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of joining: separate stars are drawn into a figure, that figure becomes a bounded region, a sign, a set of symptoms, a crowd of notables, a satellite network, a naming grid and finally any arrangement of circumstances.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「连合」动作展开：分开的星被连成一个图形；这个图形再变成有边界的区域、一个宫、一组症状、一批名人、一张卫星网、一套命名格，最后变成任何境况的组合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bright points joined by imagined lines until a figure appears in the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：亮着的点被想象中的线连起来，天空浮出一个图形。

branches.en: THE FIGURE AND ITS USE AS A NAME: the pattern, and the surname it gives to stars.
branches.cn: 图形及其命名用途：图案本身，以及它给恒星的姓。

branches.en: TWO OFFICIAL SYSTEMS: the bordered region of astronomy and the sign of astrology.
branches.cn: 两套正式体系：天文的有界区域与占星的宫。

branches.en: A SET SEEN AS ONE: symptoms, interests, any arrangement that only works together.
branches.cn: 被看成一体的集合：症状、利益，任何只有凑在一起才成立的排列。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL SKY: a room of distinguished people read as stars.
branches.cn: 社交的天空：一屋子显赫人物被读成星星。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERED SKY: satellites coordinated into one pattern.
branches.cn: 工程化的天空：卫星被协调成一个图形。

intro.en: Constellation is a Latin compound of a prefix, a star root and a noun suffix; each piece is still productive in English.
intro.cn: constellation 是拉丁复合词，由前缀、星词根与名词后缀构成；每一部分在英语中仍有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin stella also gives stellar and constellate, while Greek aster supplies the parallel set asterisk, asteroid and asterism.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stella 还给出 stellar 与 constellate，而希腊 aster 提供平行的一组：asterisk、asteroid、asterism。

items.example: The prefix gathers the stars into one set.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把星聚成一组。

items.example: The root is shared with stellar.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 stellar 共享。

items.example: Constellatio is the result of being set with stars.
items.exampleCN: constellatio 指被布满星之后的状态。
晚期拉丁语造出这个名词。

items.example: English keeps the Latin shape almost unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 英语几乎原样保留了拉丁词形。

items.meaning: to set with stars; to gather
items.example: Rare in English but alive in the family.
items.exampleCN: 英语中罕见，但词族仍在。

items.example: Greek aster is a cousin, not a parent.
items.exampleCN: 希腊 aster 是表亲，不是父母。

items.example: The modern compound satellite constellation uses the borrowed sense.
items.exampleCN: 现代复合词 satellite constellation 用的正是这层借义。

definition_zh: 组成部分；成分；构成要素；选民；（形容词）构成的、有制宪权的
definition_en: one of the parts that together make up a whole; a voter in a district; as an adjective, forming or helping to establish something
core_image: 一块块砖被砌进同一面墙：每块砖都是墙的组成部分
scene: 这组词中，At the constituent assembly, delegates argued over how the new state should be built.
sceneCN: 这里 constituent 是「制宪的」（第 3 个义项：制宪会议）；句意：在制宪会议上，代表们争论新国家应当如何建立。图中可辨识物件：会议长桌、国旗草案、代表证、投票箱。

pos.zh: 构成的；组成整体的；有制宪权的

derivatives.zh: 宪法的；符合宪法的；体质的

senses.title: A part that makes up a whole
senses.titleCN: 组成部分：构成整体的一部分
senses.definition: one of the separate parts that together form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 共同构成一个整体的各个部分之一
senses.example: Each constituent of the machine can be replaced separately.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器的每个组成部分都可以单独更换。
senses.why: Constituent comes from Latin constituens, the present participle of constituere 'to set up, establish'. A constituent is literally 'a thing set into' a larger whole: it has been placed in the structure and helps hold it up.
senses.whyCN: constituent 来自拉丁语 constituens，即 constituere“设立、建立”的现在分词。组成部分字面上就是“被安置进”更大整体中的东西：它被放进结构里，并帮助撑起结构。

senses.title: A substance that forms part of a mixture
senses.titleCN: 物质成分：混合物中的某种成分
senses.definition: a substance that is one of the materials making up a mixture or structure
senses.definitionCN: 构成混合物或结构的一种材料
senses.example: Calcium is a key constituent of bone.
senses.exampleCN: 钙是骨骼的一种关键成分。
senses.why: The same 'set into' image applies to matter: a chemical constituent has been placed into the mixture and is part of its make-up. The -ent form names the thing that has been constituted into the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“被安置进去”的形象也适用于物质：化学成分被放进混合物，成为其组成的一部分。-ent 形式命名那个被构成进整体的东西。

senses.title: Constituent assembly: a body that sets up a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪会议：设立国家的机构
senses.definition: a specially elected assembly whose task is to draw up a constitution
senses.definitionCN: 为起草宪法而专门选出的代表会议
senses.example: The constituent assembly drafted the new republic's charter.
senses.exampleCN: 制宪会议起草了新共和国的宪章。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the verb's active force: a constituent assembly is an assembly that constitutes, that sets up the state's fundamental order. Here the word describes the setting-up act itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了动词的主动力量：constituent assembly 就是“进行构成”的会议，它设立国家的基本秩序。这里这个词描述的是“设立”这一行为本身。

senses.title: Constituent country: a unit inside a union
senses.titleCN: 构成国：联合体内的组成单位
senses.definition: a country or state that forms part of a larger political union, such as the United Kingdom
senses.definitionCN: 构成更大政治联合体（如英国）的一部分的国家或地区
senses.example: Scotland is a constituent country of the United Kingdom.
senses.exampleCN: 苏格兰是英国的构成国。
senses.why: A constituent country is a country that helps constitute a larger state. The same participle logic applies: it is a unit set into the union. Note that the voting district itself is a constituency, not a constituent.
senses.whyCN: 构成国是帮助构成更大国家的国家。同样的分词逻辑：它是被安置进联合体的单位。注意：选区本身是 constituency，而不是 constituent。

senses.title: A grammatical unit in a sentence
senses.titleCN: 语法成分：句子中的结构单位
senses.definition: a word or group of words that functions as a single unit within a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 在句子中作为一个单位起作用的词或词组
senses.example: In 'the old bridge', the whole phrase is a constituent of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 在 the old bridge 中，整个短语是句子的一个成分。
senses.why: Modern linguistics borrowed the word for structure: a constituent is a piece 'set into' a larger sentence and can be moved or replaced as a unit. The Latin 'standing in a structure' sense becomes grammatical analysis.
senses.whyCN: 现代语言学借这个词来描述结构：语法成分是“被安置进”更大句子的片段，可以作为一个单位移动或替换。拉丁语“站在结构中”的意思变成了语法分析。

senses.title: An essential element of a concept or situation
senses.titleCN: 构成要素：使事物成立的关键元素
senses.definition: an element that is necessary for something to exist or be what it is
senses.definitionCN: 某事物存在或成为自身所必需的元素
senses.example: Trust is a constituent element of a healthy partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是健康合作关系的一个构成要素。
senses.why: The word moves from physical parts to abstract ones. A constituent element is still something 'set into' the whole, but now the whole is a relationship or idea rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物质部分转向抽象部分。构成要素仍然是“被安置进”整体的东西，只是这个整体现在是关系或观念，而不是物体。

senses.title: A voter in a district
senses.titleCN: 选民：选区中有投票权的人
senses.definition: a person who lives in an electoral district and has the right to vote there
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一选区并有投票权的人
senses.example: The senator met with constituents at the town hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参议员在市政厅会见选民。
senses.why: In political usage the person 'constitutes' the electorate: voters set up the representative body. The noun shifted from 'one who constitutes' to 'one who is represented', a concrete political role.
senses.whyCN: 在政治用法中，个人“构成”选民群体：选民设立了代议机构。名词从“构成者”转为“被代表者”，成为一个具体的政治角色。

senses.title: Constituent power: the authority to found a state
senses.titleCN: 制宪权：创立国家的权力
senses.definition: the ultimate authority of a people to establish or change its constitution
senses.definitionCN: 人民设立或改变其宪法的终极权力
senses.example: The court debated whether the people hold constituent power.
senses.exampleCN: 法院讨论了人民是否拥有制宪权。
senses.why: Here the adjective names the power that constitutes: the capacity to set up the legal order itself. It is the most abstract extension of constituere 'establish', applied to the founding act rather than to a part.
senses.whyCN: 这里形容词命名“进行构成”的权力：设立法律秩序本身的能力。这是 constituere“建立”最抽象的延伸，作用于创立行为而非某个部分。

senses.title: Constituent structure: the arrangement of parts
senses.titleCN: 成分结构：各部分的层级组织
senses.definition: the hierarchical arrangement of parts within a sentence or system
senses.definitionCN: 句子或系统内部各部分的层级排列方式
senses.example: The tree diagram shows the constituent structure of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 树形图展示了这个句子的成分结构。
senses.why: Structure names the way constituents are set together. The word keeps its compositional sense but now describes the whole arrangement rather than any single part; -ent still marks the unit that has been set in.
senses.whyCN: 结构命名各成分被放在一起的方式。这个词保留组合义，但现在描述整体排列而非单个部分；-ent 仍标记那个被安置进去的单位。

intro.en: Constituent is a Latin present participle in -ent, from constituere 'set up, establish'. The base verb splits into con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: constituent 是带 -ent 的拉丁语现在分词，来自 constituere“设立、建立”。基础动词拆为 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Constituere means 'to set up, establish, appoint, constitute'. It is a compound of con- 'together' and statuere 'to place, set, fix'.
items.cn: constituere 意为“设立、建立、任命、构成”。它由 con-“一起”和 statuere“放置、设立、固定”复合而成。

items.en: Its present participle is constituens, stem constituent-, 'setting up; that which sets up'. This is the exact form English borrows, so the word arrives already carrying the active idea of putting something in place.
items.cn: 它的现在分词是 constituens，词干 constituent-，意为“正在设立的；设立者”。英语借用的正是这一形式，因此这个词一进入英语就带着“把某物安放到位”的主动含义。

items.en: The -ent suffix (Latin -ent-) makes an adjective or noun from the participle. As an adjective, constituent means 'forming part of'; as a noun, 'the thing that constitutes' or 'one who constitutes'.
items.cn: 后缀 -ent（拉丁语 -ent-）把分词变成形容词或名词。作形容词时 constituent 意为“构成部分的”；作名词时意为“构成之物”或“构成者”。

items.en: English adopts constituent in the 16c. as both adjective and noun, first in the general sense 'forming part of a whole'. The political senses grow from the idea of parts that set up a larger body.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪引入 constituent，形容词与名词并用，最初是一般义“构成整体的一部分”。政治义从“设立更大机构的部分”这一观念生长出来。

items.en: By the 18c. a constituent is 'a person who has the right to elect a representative'. The voter is the person who constitutes the representative body, so the noun moves from maker to member of the electorate.
items.cn: 到 18 世纪，constituent 指“有权选举代表的人”。选民是构成代议机构的人，因此名词从“构成者”转为“选民群体的一员”。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense (a constituent of a mixture), the political senses (constituent assembly, constituent power, voter), and the 20c. linguistic sense of a syntactic unit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物质义（混合物的成分）、政治义（制宪会议、制宪权、选民），以及 20 世纪语言学的句法单位义。

note.en: The first group holds same-family words that are often confused with constituent; the second holds nouns that also name a part of a whole.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 constituent 混淆的同族词；第二组是同样表示“整体的一部分”的名词。

entries.definition: a voting district or the voters in it. It is the place or group, while a constituent is one voter.
entries.definitionCN: 选区或该区选民。它是地区或群体，而 constituent 是其中一位选民。

entries.definition: to form or make up something; to establish. It is the verb behind constituent.
entries.definitionCN: 构成某物；设立。它是 constituent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: the fundamental law of a state, or the make-up of a body. It is the -tion noun from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 国家的根本法，或身体的构成。它是同一动词加 -tion 的名词。

entries.definition: a part of a larger machine or system. It is close to constituent but more common in technical contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 较大机器或系统的一部分。它与 constituent 接近，但更常用于技术语境。

entries.definition: one of the basic parts of something. It is broader and can be abstract or chemical.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物的基本部分之一。它更宽泛，可指抽象要素或化学元素。

entries.definition: one of the foods or substances combined to make something. It is mostly used for cooking and mixtures.
entries.definitionCN: 组合成某物的食材或物质之一。它多用于烹饪和混合物。

entries.definition: a piece of a whole. It is the everyday word that constituent formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分。它是 constituent 所正式化的日常词。

entries.definition: one element that contributes to a result. It is about influence rather than physical make-up.
entries.definitionCN: 促成结果的一个要素。它讲的是影响，而不是物理构成。

normalIntro.en: These links use the real constituere family, the real -ent participle ending, and real political collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联系使用真实的 constituere 词族、真实的分词后缀 -ent，以及真实政治搭配。

normal.en: con- 'together' + statuere 'set' + -ent 'the one doing': a constituent is a thing set into the whole.
normal.cn: con-“一起” + statuere“放置” + -ent“做此事者”：constituent 就是被安置进整体的东西。

normal.en: Keep the family apart: constitute is the verb, constituent is a part or voter, constitution is the fundamental law, constituency is the district.
normal.cn: 分清词族：constitute 是动词，constituent 是部分或选民，constitution 是根本法，constituency 是选区。

normal.en: The political phrases are fixed: constituent assembly, constituent power, constituent country.
normal.cn: 政治短语是固定的：constituent assembly、constituent power、constituent country。

normal.en: A constituent is one voter; all the voters together form a constituency. One letter changes the unit.
normal.cn: 一位选民是 constituent；全体选民构成 constituency。一个字母之差，单位就变了。

normal.en: In grammar, a constituent is any word or phrase that can stand as a unit inside a larger sentence.
normal.cn: 在语法中，成分是任何能在更大句子中作为一个单位站立的词或短语。

abstract.en: Picture a wall: each brick is set into it and helps hold it up. That brick is a constituent; the wall is the whole.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙：每块砖都被砌进去，并帮助撑住墙。那块砖就是 constituent，墙则是整体。

abstract.en: The word always implies placement. A constituent is not just nearby; it has been put in and is part of the structure.
abstract.cn: 这个词总含有“被安放”的意味。组成部分不是仅仅在旁边，而是被放进去、成为结构的一部分。

abstract.en: The voter sense keeps the same logic: voters are the pieces that set up the representative body.
abstract.cn: 选民义保留同一逻辑：选民是设立代议机构的那些“部件”。

examples.en: Protein is a major constituent of every living cell.
examples.cn: 蛋白质是每个活细胞的主要成分。

examples.en: The constituent assembly began drafting the constitution in 1787.
examples.cn: 制宪会议于 1787 年开始起草宪法。

examples.en: The representative holds a weekly meeting with her constituents.
examples.cn: 这位代表每周与她的选民会面。

dict_mnemonic.text: “肯斯提球恩特”——肯斯提把球摁特进墙里，每块砖都是组成部分 → constituent 成分

root: 拉丁 constituere“设立、放置”（con- 一起 + statuere 放置）+ -ent（分词后缀）：被安置进整体、构成本身的那一部分。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of constituent all come from 'something set into a whole'. The whole may be a machine, a mixture, a state, a sentence, a relationship, or an electorate.
sensesIntro.cn: constituent 的九个义项都来自“被安置进整体的东西”。这个整体可以是机器、混合物、国家、句子、关系或选民群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brick set into a wall, each brick helping to hold the wall up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块块砖被砌进同一面墙，每块砖都帮助撑住墙。

branches.en: PART AND ELEMENT: a concrete part of a whole, and an essential element of an idea or situation.
branches.cn: 部分与要素：整体的具体部分，以及观念或情境中不可缺少的元素。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND STRUCTURE: a substance inside a mixture, and the arrangement of all the parts.
branches.cn: 物质与结构：混合物中的物质成分，以及所有部分的排列方式。

branches.en: FOUNDING: an assembly that sets up a state, and the ultimate power to do so.
branches.cn: 创立：设立国家的会议，以及这样做的终极权力。

branches.en: POLITICAL MEMBERSHIP: a unit inside a union, and a voter inside a district.
branches.cn: 政治成员：联合体内部的组成单位，以及选区内部的选民。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word or phrase functioning as one structural unit.
branches.cn: 语法：作为一个结构单位起作用的词或短语。

intro.en: Constituent is built from the Latin participle constituens. English adds no new prefix here; the -ent ending is the same suffix that makes adjectives such as consistent and different.
intro.cn: constituent 由拉丁语分词 constituens 构成。英语在这里没有再加新前缀；-ent 就是构成 consistent、different 等形容词的同一个后缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is constituere, from con- 'together' + statuere 'place, set'. Constituens is its present participle, and the -ent- stem is what English borrows.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是 constituere，来自 con-“一起” + statuere“放置、设立”。constituens 是它的现在分词，英语借用的就是 -ent- 词干。

items.meaning: to form, make up, or establish
items.meaningCN: 构成；设立（con- 表示“一起”）
items.exampleCN: 十二名成员构成了这个委员会。

items.meaning: a part that makes up a whole
items.meaningCN: 组成部分；成分（-ent 分词后缀）
items.example: Water is a constituent of every cell.

items.meaning: the fundamental law or make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 宪法；体质；构成（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The country adopted a new constitution.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家通过了新宪法。

items.meaningCN: 宪法的；合宪的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The court reviewed the constitutional question.
items.exampleCN: 法院审查了这个宪法问题。

items.meaning: a voting district or its voters
items.meaningCN: 选区；选民群体（-cy 构成名词）
items.example: The candidate visited every town in the constituency.
items.exampleCN: 候选人走访了选区的每个城镇。

items.meaning: more than one part or voter
items.meaningCN: 多个组成部分或选民（复数后缀）
items.example: The medicine contains several active constituents.
items.exampleCN: 这种药含有几种活性成分。

items.meaning: formed or established in the past
items.meaningCN: 构成了；设立了（过去式／过去分词）

items.example: The fields constituting the park are protected.
items.exampleCN: 构成公园的那些田地受到保护。

items.meaning: essential to the make-up of something
items.meaningCN: 构成的；本质性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: Language is a constitutive part of human culture.
items.exampleCN: 语言是人类文化的构成性部分。

latinEntries.meaning: setting up; that which sets up

latinEntries.meaningCN: 表示具有某种性质或执行某动作的

definition_zh: 构成；算是；设立
definition_en: to form or make up something, or to establish it officially
core_image: 几块砖被摆成一个明确的形状，成为一堵墙
scene: 老师指着实验台上的几样器材说明用途。These small parts constitute the whole system.
sceneCN: 这里 constitute 指「构成」（第 1 个义项：若干部分组成整体）；句意是这些小部件构成了整个系统。

senses.title: Make up a whole
senses.definition: to form a whole when the parts are taken together
senses.definitionCN: 各部分合起来形成一个整体
senses.example: Ten chapters constitute the whole book.
senses.exampleCN: 十章构成了整本书。
senses.why: A whole is only a name until its parts are counted.
senses.whyCN: 整体在数清部分之前，只是一个名字。

senses.title: Amount to something
senses.definition: to be serious or important enough to count as something
senses.definitionCN: 严重或重要到足以被算作某事
senses.example: Such neglect may constitute a crime.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疏忽可能构成犯罪。
senses.why: Law needs a line where a behaviour becomes a named act.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一条界线，让某种行为变成有名字的罪行。

senses.title: Set up officially
senses.definition: to establish an official body by formal act
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式程序建立官方机构
senses.example: They constituted a committee to study the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设立了一个委员会来研究此案。
senses.why: A group becomes an institution on the day it is written down.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体在被写下来的那天，才成为机构。

intro.en: Constitute comes from Latin constituere, to set up or appoint, built from com-, together, and statuere, to place.
intro.cn: constitute 来自拉丁语 constituere，意为设立或任命，由 com-（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成。

items.en: Statuere meant to set something in place and make it stand.
items.cn: statuere 意为把某物放好并让它立住。

items.en: Constituere meant to set up a body or appoint an officer.
items.cn: constituere 意为设立机构或任命官员。

items.en: The noun constitutio named an arrangement and later a decree.
items.cn: 名词 constitutio 指安排，后来指法令。

items.en: French constituer used the word for founding and composing.
items.cn: 法语 constituer 用它表示创立与组成。

items.en: English constitute meant to establish an official body.
items.cn: 英语 constitute 最初指设立官方机构。

items.en: It now commonly means to make up or amount to something.
items.cn: 如今它常表示构成或等同于某事。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin statu- base, and the meaning group names other verbs for making up a whole.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 statu- 词基，近义组列出其他表示构成整体的动词。

entries.definition: the basic laws of a state, or the way something is made
one of the parts that make up a whole
to start an official system or organization
to form the parts of a whole
to consist of particular parts
to make something into a shape or body

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from bricks set into one wall, then move to an act heavy enough to count as a crime and to a body written into being.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从砌成一堵墙的砖开始，再到重到足以算作犯罪的行为，最后到被写出来的机构。

normal.en: Con- is together and stitute is set up, so constitute is setting things up into one body.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，stitute 是设立，constitute 就是把东西搭成一个整体。

normal.en: Bricks do not become a wall until they are counted together.
normal.cn: 砖要一起被数清，才变成一堵墙。

normal.en: A small act can constitute a big charge in a court.
normal.cn: 一个小动作，在法庭上可能构成重罪。

normal.en: To constitute a committee is to write a group into being.
normal.cn: 设立一个委员会，就是把一群人写进现实。

normal.en: First the parts, then the name of the whole.
normal.cn: 先有部分，再有整体的名字。

abstract.en: Picture several blocks locked into one clear shape.
abstract.cn: 想象几块积木扣成一个清晰的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a line of names signed under a new rule.
abstract.cn: 想象一条新规下面签着一排名字。

abstract.en: Picture one drop joining others to make a stream.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水与其他水汇成一条小溪。

examples.en: Women constitute half of the workforce here.
examples.cn: 女性构成了这里劳动力的一半。

examples.en: Driving without lights may constitute an offence.
examples.cn: 不开灯驾驶可能构成违法。

examples.en: The members constituted a new council last spring.
examples.cn: 成员们在去年春天组建了一个新理事会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constitute 记成 con（一起）加 stitute（设立）：把若干部分一起立起来，就成了一个整体，即构成。

root: 源自拉丁语 constituere（com 一起 + statuere 放置），本义是把东西一起立起来，后指构成整体、等同于某事与正式设立。

sensesIntro.en: From parts forming a whole, to an act serious enough to be named, and at last to a body set up by formal words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从部分形成整体，到严重到足以被命名的行为，最后到用正式文字设立的机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bricks set down one by one until a wall stands.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖一块块放好，直到一堵墙立起来。

branches.en: The first sense simply joins parts into one named whole.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是把部分合成一个有名字的整体。

branches.en: The second sense says an act is heavy enough to be renamed as an offence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项说某行为重到可以被改称为一项罪名。

branches.en: The third sense writes a group into official existence.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把一个群体写进正式的建制。

branches.en: Both senses turn separate pieces into something with a legal name.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把分散的片段变成有正式名称的东西。

branches.en: A court and a council both depend on words that constitute.
branches.cn: 法庭与理事会都依靠那些起构成作用的文字。

intro.en: Constitute is built on Latin con-, together, plus statuere, to set in place.
intro.cn: constitute 由拉丁语 con-（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin set base stitut- also appears in constitution, institute and substitute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的放置词基 stitut- 也出现在 constitution、institute 与 substitute 中。

items.meaning: to set parts up into one whole
items.example: These twelve poems constitute the collection.
items.exampleCN: 这十二首诗构成了这本诗集。

items.meaning: the way something is built, or a state's basic law
items.meaningCN: 构成方式，或国家的根本法

items.example: The court called the rule constitutional.
items.exampleCN: 法院认定该规定符合宪法。

items.meaning: one part that helps form a whole
items.example: Water is the main constituent of the drink.
items.exampleCN: 水是这种饮料的主要成分。

items.meaning: to set a system in place
items.example: They instituted a new safety rule.
items.exampleCN: 他们设立了一条新的安全规定。

items.meaning: a law set down in writing
a figure set up to stand
to put one thing in place of another
items.meaningCN: 把一物放到另一物的位置
items.example: You can substitute honey for sugar.

definition_zh: 宪法；构成；体质
definition_en: the basic laws of a country, the way something is made up, or a person's health
core_image: 一本薄薄的册子，写着国家如何运转
scene: 开学第一课，老师讲国家的基本大法。The constitution limits the power of the government.
sceneCN: 这里 constitution 指「宪法」（第 1 个义项：国家的根本大法）；句意是宪法限制政府的权力。

senses.title: The basic law
senses.definition: the set of rules that a country is governed by
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家据以治理的根本规则
senses.example: The constitution protects freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 宪法保护言论自由。
senses.why: A nation needs one page that other pages must obey.
senses.whyCN: 一个国家需要一页让其他各页都必须服从的文字。

senses.title: How something is made
senses.definition: the way the parts of something are put together
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的各个部分拼合的方式
senses.example: Scientists studied the constitution of the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家研究了土壤的构成。
senses.why: To know a thing you must know what holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 要认识一件事物，就得知道是什么把它拢在一起。

senses.title: A person's build
senses.definition: the natural health and strength of a body
senses.definitionCN: 身体天生的健康与强健程度
senses.example: He has a strong constitution and rarely falls ill.
senses.exampleCN: 他体质强健，很少生病。
senses.why: The same word that builds a state also builds a body.
senses.whyCN: 搭建国家的那同一个词，也用来搭建身体。

intro.en: Constitution comes from Latin constitutio, a setting in order, from constituere, to set up, built on com- and statuere, to place.
intro.cn: constitution 来自拉丁语 constitutio，意为安排、规定，源自 constituere（设立），由 com- 与 statuere（放置）构成。

items.en: Statuere meant to place something so that it stands.
items.cn: statuere 意为把某物放好使它立住。

items.en: Constitutio named the way a thing was ordered and arranged.
items.cn: constitutio 指事物被安排与组织的方式。

items.en: Roman writers used it for an official decree.
items.cn: 罗马作家用它指官方的法令。

items.en: French constitution carried the sense of a settled arrangement.
items.cn: 法语 constitution 带有既定安排的含义。

items.en: English constitution first meant the makeup of body or mind.
items.cn: 英语 constitution 最初指身体或心智的构造。

items.en: It became the standard word for a nation's fundamental law.
items.cn: 它成为指国家根本大法的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin statu- base, and the meaning group names other words for a founding set of rules.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语 statu- 词基，近义组列出其他表示立国规则的词。

entries.definition: to make up or formally establish something
a part that helps form a whole
an established organization or custom
a formal document granting rights
a rule that a society must obey
the way parts are arranged together

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from one thin book of rules, then move to the way parts are fitted and to the strength of a body.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一本薄薄的规则册子开始，再到部件拼合的方式，最后到身体的强健。

normal.en: Con- is together and stitute is set up, so a constitution is everything set up together as one order.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，stitute 是设立，constitution 就是被一起立成一套秩序的东西。

normal.en: The nation's rulebook fits into one pocket.
normal.cn: 整个国家的规则手册，能放进一个口袋。

normal.en: The constitution of a soil and of a state use the same word for a reason.
normal.cn: 土壤的构成与国家的宪法用同一个词，是有原因的。

normal.en: A strong constitution keeps a body running without complaint.
normal.cn: 强健的体质让身体不吭声地运转。

normal.en: Ask what it is made of, and you are asking about its constitution.
normal.cn: 问它由什么构成，问的就是它的构成。

abstract.en: Picture a small book placed above all other books.
abstract.cn: 想象一本小书被放在所有其他书上头。

abstract.en: Picture a wall with every brick named in a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙，每块砖都在图纸上有名字。

abstract.en: Picture a body walking uphill without stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体走上坡路而不停下。

examples.en: The new constitution was approved by a wide margin.
examples.cn: 新宪法以很大优势获得通过。

examples.en: The constitution of the committee changed last year.
examples.cn: 委员会的构成去年发生了变化。

examples.en: Years of running gave her a tough constitution.
examples.cn: 多年跑步让她有了强健的体质。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 constitution 记成 con（一起）加 stitute（设立）加 ion：把一个国家的根本规则一起立起来，就是宪法。

root: 源自拉丁语 constitutio（安排、规定），词根 constituere 由 com（一起）与 statuere（放置）构成，本义是一起立定，后指宪法、构成与体质。

sensesIntro.en: From one book of rules, to the fit of parts inside a thing, and to the build of a living body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一本规则之书，到事物内部部件的拼合，最后到活人身体的底子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin book that all other rules must answer to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本薄书，其他一切规则都要向它交代。

branches.en: The first sense is the rulebook that outranks every other rule.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是压过其他一切规则的规则书。

branches.en: The second sense asks how the parts of a thing are arranged.
branches.cn: 第二个义项问的是一件事物的部件如何排布。

branches.en: The third sense applies the same idea to a living body.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把同一个想法用到活人身上。

branches.en: Both senses describe a whole held together by an inner order.
branches.cn: 两个义项都描述靠内在秩序拢住的整体。

branches.en: A body and a state are both judged by how well they are built.
branches.cn: 身体与国家都要看底子搭得好不好。

intro.en: Constitution is built on Latin con-, together, plus statuere, to place, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: constitution 由拉丁语 con-（一起）、statuere（放置）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin place base stitut- also appears in constitute, institute and substitute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的放置词基 stitut- 也出现在 constitute、institute 与 substitute 中。

items.meaning: the settled order of a state or a thing
items.meaningCN: 国家或事物既定的秩序
items.example: The constitution was signed in the hall.
items.exampleCN: 宪法在那座大厅里签署。

items.meaning: to set parts up into a whole

items.exampleCN: 他们提出了宪法层面的诉求。

items.meaning: in a way that follows the basic law
items.exampleCN: 这一举措在宪法上站得住。

items.example: The court struck down the unconstitutional rule.
items.exampleCN: 法院废除了那条违宪的规定。

items.meaning: a part that builds a whole
items.exampleCN: 每个组成部分各有一票。

items.meaning: to put a system in place
items.exampleCN: 他们设立了一套审查程序。

items.example: The statute took effect in May.
